name: UNLDGSAM.JCL
description:
This JCL job (UNLDGSAM) executes an IMS DL/I batch program (DBUNLDGS) using the IMS region controller (DFSRRC00) to unload data from an IMS Payment Authorization database (PAUTHDB) into two GSAM (Generalized Sequential Access Method) output files — one for root segments and one for child segments — as part of the CardDemo application's data migration or extract process.Key Functionalities:
Executes the IMS DL/I batch unload program (DBUNLDGS) using PSB DLIGSAMP to read from the IMS Payment Authorization database (PAUTHDB)
Unloads IMS root segment records from the Payment Authorization database into a sequential GSAM output file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PAUTDB.ROOT.GSAM), retaining the file after the job completes
Unloads IMS child segment records from the Payment Authorization database into a separate sequential GSAM output file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PAUTDB.CHILD.GSAM), retaining the file after the job completes
Reads the IMS Payment Authorization primary database (OEM.IMS.IMSP.PAUTHDB) and its index (OEM.IMS.IMSP.PAUTHDBX) as source data for the unload operation
Utilizes IMS PSB and DBD libraries to define the program's database access structure and segment layouts during execution

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The IMS Payment Authorization Database (PAUTHDB) contains payment authorization records organized in a hierarchical structure with root/parent records and child/dependent records, AND the PSB DLIGSAMP is available to define the authorized access scope for the unload program DBUNLDGS
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The DBUNLDGS program is executed in IMS DL/I batch mode to perform a full unload of the entire Payment Authorization Database with no filtering or selection criteria applied
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All root/parent Payment Authorization records are written exclusively to the ROOT GSAM output file (PASFILOP — AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PAUTDB.ROOT.GSAM), AND all child/dependent Payment Authorization records are written exclusively to the CHILD GSAM output file (PADFILOP — AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PAUTDB.CHILD.GSAM), ensuring every record in the database is extracted and the parent-child relationship is preserved across the two output files

rules.Rule_Name: STEP01 - DFSRRC00 - Payment Authorization Database Full Extraction with Hierarchical Record Separation
rules.Rule_Description: The IMS batch program DBUNLDGS performs a complete unload of all records from the Payment Authorization Database and separates them into two output files — one for root/parent records and one for child/dependent records — preserving the hierarchical business relationship across flat files.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Payment Authorization Database unload job (UNLDGSAM) is initiated and STEP01 is about to execute
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The job attempts to open the ROOT GSAM file (PASFILOP — AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PAUTDB.ROOT.GSAM) and the CHILD GSAM file (PADFILOP — AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PAUTDB.CHILD.GSAM) for writing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Both files must already exist in the system prior to job execution; if the ROOT GSAM file does not exist, the job fails immediately before any data extraction begins; if the CHILD GSAM file does not exist, the job fails immediately before any data extraction begins; no new files are created by this job

rules.Rule_Name: STEP01 - DFSRRC00 - Output File Pre-existence Validation for Payment Authorization Unload
rules.Rule_Description: Both output files designated to receive the extracted Payment Authorization records must already exist in the system before the unload job begins. The job does not create these files — it only writes into pre-existing ones.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Payment Authorization Database unload is executing and actively writing extracted records to the ROOT GSAM file (PASFILOP) and the CHILD GSAM file (PADFILOP)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The job completes — either successfully with all records fully extracted, OR abnormally due to an error or failure at any point during processing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: On successful completion — both output files are retained in the system containing the complete set of extracted Payment Authorization records; On abnormal termination — both output files are still retained in the system but may contain only a partial set of records extracted up to the point of failure; downstream processes consuming these files must independently verify data completeness before use, as the job does not purge or reset partial output on failure

rules.Rule_Name: STEP01 - DFSRRC00 - Payment Authorization Output File Retention Policy
rules.Rule_Description: Both Payment Authorization output files — ROOT GSAM and CHILD GSAM — are retained in the system regardless of whether the unload job completes successfully or terminates with a failure, which may result in partial data being preserved in the event of a failure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Payment Authorization Database unload job is actively running and reading records from the Payment Authorization Database (DDPAUTP0 — PAUTHDB) and its index (DDPAUTX0 — PAUTHDBX)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Other business applications or batch jobs need to access the Payment Authorization Database at the same time as the unload is in progress
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The unload operation accesses the database in shared mode and does not acquire exclusive locks; other authorized users and processes can simultaneously read from the Payment Authorization Database without interruption; the unload does not block, delay, or prevent concurrent access to the Payment Authorization Database or its index

rules.Rule_Name: STEP01 - DFSRRC00 - Concurrent Shared Access to Payment Authorization Database During Unload
rules.Rule_Description: The Payment Authorization Database and its index are accessed in shared mode during the unload operation, ensuring that other business applications and batch jobs can continue to access the same database simultaneously without being blocked.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The DBUNLDGS program is initializing its connection to the IMS Payment Authorization Database through the IMS DL/I interface, AND the PSB library (PSBLIB) and Database Definition library (DBDLIB) are available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program establishes its database session and begins reading records from the Payment Authorization Database
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Access is authorized and scoped exclusively by PSB DLIGSAMP; only the database segments (record types) defined and permitted within DLIGSAMP are accessible to the unload program; the program reads segments only in the sequence and manner authorized by DLIGSAMP; any segment not defined in DLIGSAMP is inaccessible to the program

rules.Rule_Name: STEP01 - DFSRRC00 - PSB-Based Authorization for Payment Authorization Database Access
rules.Rule_Description: Access to the Payment Authorization Database during the unload is governed and restricted by PSB DLIGSAMP, which defines the specific record types (segments) the unload program is authorized to read and the sequence in which they are accessed.
